research_question: In adult smokers, what is the effect of an Internet-based smoking cessation intervention combined with behavioural support, compared with a non-Internet-based non-active control, on smoking cessation at 6 months or longer follow-up?
treatment_label: Internet-based smoking cessation intervention combined with behavioural support
outcome_description: Smoking cessation/abstinence assessed at 6 months or longer follow-up, using the study's most rigorous reported definition of abstinence (biochemically verified continuous/prolonged abstinence preferred over point prevalence self-report).
positive_direction: A positive effect (Risk Ratio > 1) indicates a higher rate of smoking cessation/abstinence in the Internet-based intervention with behavioural support group compared to the non-active control group.
search_queries: internet smoking cessation behavioral support trial outcome
web-based tobacco cessation counseling controlled trial abstinence
online smoking cessation program behavioral support randomized trial
inclusion_criteria: Studies evaluating adult smokers receiving an Internet-based smoking cessation intervention combined with behavioural support compared with a non-Internet-based non-active control (e.g., waitlist, usual care, brief printed self-help).
Studies reporting quantitative dichotomous outcomes for smoking cessation or abstinence at 6 months or longer follow-up.
Controlled comparative empirical studies (e.g., randomized controlled trials, quasi-randomized trials, or controlled clinical trials).
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, protocols, editorials, opinion pieces, and theoretical papers are excluded).
No comparison between an Internet-based smoking cessation intervention with behavioural support and a non-Internet-based non-active control condition.
No quantitative outcome data on smoking cessation/abstinence at 6 months or longer follow-up that can produce a risk ratio or dichotomous event counts.
Studies reporting only short-term outcomes (<6 months) or completely unrelated to smoking cessation.
moderators_to_extract: Abstinence definition (continuous/prolonged abstinence vs point prevalence abstinence)
Biochemical verification status (biochemically validated vs self-report only)
Duration of follow-up (6 months vs 12 months or longer)
Format/intensity of behavioural support (human-delivered counseling vs automated tailored messages)
Control condition type (waitlist, usual care, no intervention, self-help leaflet)
effect_size_note: Extract the most rigorous reported definition of abstinence for this comparison (prioritising biochemically verified continuous or prolonged abstinence over self-reported point prevalence abstinence), using one endpoint per study at the longest available follow-up ≥6 months. Dichotomous outcome pooled using Risk Ratio (RR).
single_outcome_target: smoking cessation at 6 months or longer
